theorem_title: Theorem D as a barrier: some ℚ-subspace L ⊇ ℒ of ℂ has all the Theorem D properties and contains u ≠ 0 with |u| algebraic
formal_statement:
open Complex ComplexConjugate

namespace DiazModulus

theorem theorem_D_barrier :
    ∃ L : Submodule ℚ ℂ, (∀ z ∈ LogAlg, z ∈ L) ∧
      /- conjugation -/
      (∀ z ∈ L, conj z ∈ L) ∧
      /- (D2) Baker -/
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (l : Fin n → ℂ), (∀ i, l i ∈ L) → LinearIndependent ℚ l →
        ∀ (b₀ : ℂ) (b : Fin n → ℂ), IsAlgebraic ℚ b₀ → (∀ i, IsAlgebraic ℚ (b i)) →
          (b₀ ≠ 0 ∨ ∃ i, b i ≠ 0) → b₀ + ∑ i, b i * l i ≠ 0) ∧
      /- (D2) Hermite-Lindemann -/
      (∀ z ∈ L, IsAlgebraic ℚ z → z = 0) ∧
      /- (D2) Gel'fond-Schneider -/
      (∀ l₀ β : ℂ, l₀ ∈ L → β * l₀ ∈ L → l₀ ≠ 0 → IsAlgebraic ℚ β →
        ∃ q : ℚ, β = (q : ℂ)) ∧
      /- (D3) Roy, relative to ℒ: strong six exponentials for ℒ̃ gives it for span Q̄ (insert 1 L) -/
      ((∀ (x : Fin 2 → ℂ) (y : Fin 3 → ℂ),
          LinearIndependent (↥Qbar) x → LinearIndependent (↥Qbar) y →
          ¬ (∀ i j, x i * y j ∈ LogAlgTilde)) →
        ∀ (x : Fin 2 → ℂ) (y : Fin 3 → ℂ),
          LinearIndependent (↥Qbar) x → LinearIndependent (↥Qbar) y →
          ¬ (∀ i j, x i * y j ∈ Submodule.span Qbar (insert 1 (L : Set ℂ)))) ∧
      /- (D3) six exponentials -/
      (∀ (x : Fin 2 → ℂ) (y : Fin 3 → ℂ), LinearIndependent ℚ x → LinearIndependent ℚ y →
        ¬ (∀ i j, x i * y j ∈ L)) ∧
      /- (D4) four exponentials in transcendence degree one -/
      (∀ l₁₁ l₁₂ l₂₁ l₂₂ : ℂ, l₁₁ ∈ L → l₁₂ ∈ L → l₂₁ ∈ L → l₂₂ ∈ L →
        l₁₁ ≠ 0 → l₁₂ ≠ 0 → l₂₁ ≠ 0 → l₂₂ ≠ 0 → l₁₁ * l₂₂ = l₁₂ * l₂₁ →
        Algebra.trdeg ℚ ↥(Algebra.adjoin ℚ ({l₁₁, l₁₂, l₂₁, l₂₂} : Set ℂ)) ≤ 1 →
        (∃ a b : ℚ, ¬(a = 0 ∧ b = 0) ∧ (a : ℂ) * l₁₁ + (b : ℂ) * l₂₁ = 0 ∧ (a : ℂ) * l₁₂ + (b : ℂ) * l₂₂ = 0) ∨
        (∃ a b : ℚ, ¬(a = 0 ∧ b = 0) ∧ (a : ℂ) * l₁₁ + (b : ℂ) * l₁₂ = 0 ∧ (a : ℂ) * l₂₁ + (b : ℂ) * l₂₂ = 0)) ∧
      ∃ u ∈ L, u ≠ 0 ∧ IsAlgebraic ℚ ((‖u‖ : ℝ) : ℂ) := by
  sorry

end DiazModulus
source: Not found in the sources read. The properties are those of Theorem D (DiazModulus.logAlg_adjoin_circle_point_theorem_D): Baker's theorem (A. Baker, Linear forms in the logarithms of algebraic numbers I, Mathematika 13 (1966), 204–216); Hermite–Lindemann (Ch. Hermite 1873; F. Lindemann 1882); Gel'fond–Schneider (A. O. Gel'fond 1934; Th. Schneider 1934); the six exponentials theorem (S. Lang, Introduction to Transcendental Numbers, Addison-Wesley, 1966, chapter II; K. Ramachandra, Contributions to the theory of transcendental numbers I, II, Acta Arith. 14 (1968)); the four exponentials theorem in transcendence degree one (M. Waldschmidt, Solution du huitième problème de Schneider, J. Number Theory 5 (1973), 191–202; W. D. Brownawell, The algebraic independence of certain numbers related by the exponential function, J. Number Theory 6 (1974), 22–31), and Roy's strong six exponentials theorem (D. Roy, Matrices whose coefficients are linear forms in logarithms, J. Number Theory 41 (1992), 22–47, Cor. 2) as an implication. Uses DiazModulus.exists_circle_point_transcendental_over_logAlgTilde_closure and DiazModulus.logAlg_adjoin_circle_point_theorem_D. R19 of the Diaz modulus mission. Formal proof: Diaz modulus mission, 18 October 2026 (C. Perassi).
